title: Jev Cookbook image assets manifest
description: A recipe's assets-manifest.json: provenance, licence and attestations for every image under its assets/ folder. Required exactly when the recipe has an assets/ folder. The validator also checks what a schema cannot: every file under assets/ is listed, every listed file exists, hash, format and size match the bytes, the generator script exists in the recipe, and no image crosses splits. See docs/fixtures.md, 'Image provenance manifest'.

assets.description: One entry per image file under the recipe's assets/ folder, in any order.

asset.description: One image file: where it is, what it is, how it was made, under what licence.

path.description: Relative to the recipe folder, with forward slashes, starting 'assets/', lowercase .png/.jpg/.jpeg suffix. Letters, digits, '_', '.' and '-' only, no segment starting with '.', so it contains no '..' and cannot leave the folder. This is exactly the string an inputs.jsonl 'fields' value uses to name the image.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the file's bytes, 64 lowercase hex characters (the digest behind image_reference).

format.description: What the bytes are: PNG or JPEG (baseline).

origin.description: How the file came to exist. Only 'generated' (drawn by the recipe's own code) is allowed.

generator.description: The code that drew it: 'build_fixtures.py:draw_dialog' (a .py file in the recipe folder, which must exist, and a function name that appears in it) or 'jev_cookbook.<module>:<function>' for shared package code.

parameters.description: The arguments, seed included, that reproduce this file from the generator: any JSON object, {} if the generator takes none.

licence.description: SPDX identifier: MIT (this repository's licence) or CC0-1.0.

description.description: What the image shows, in plain words, for a reader who cannot see it.

shared_across_splits.description: Optional, default false. true allows examples in different splits to name this same image (a shared reference image); otherwise the same bytes in two splits is a leak.

attestations.description: Explicit statements by the author, all required. The validator fails unless synthetic is true and each of the others is false.

synthetic.description: Drawn by code; no camera or scan involved.

real_photo.description: Contains a real photograph or a pixel copied from one.

real_brand.description: Shows a real brand, logo, trademark or product.

real_person.description: Shows a real person or a real person's likeness.

third_party_content.description: Contains third-party artwork, screenshots, icons, fonts rendered from a non-redistributable file, or other copyrighted material.
